week1-game1:
St. Catherines 15, Franklin 14 — One run. That’s all that separated Franklin from one of the most stunning opening-week upsets in recent league memory. Instead, St. Catherines survived a 24-hit onslaught and escaped with a 15-14 victory that was anything but comfortable.

Matt Barr delivered the opening statement for the Tigers: three hits, three runs, a double, constant presence. Anthony DeLosSantos matched the energy at the bottom of the order with a 3-for-3 night and a game-high 4 RBIs. Jerry Ng was perfect from the leadoff spot. Ten of 13 St. Catherines batters reached base at least once. For a team that finished 0-9-1 just two seasons ago, this wasn’t just a win — it was a declaration.

But Franklin refused to fold. Todd Lanam, Uland Wong, and Mu Jing each went 4-for-4, turning the middle of the lineup into a run factory. Ryan Pierce had both a double and a triple on the same night. Jason Sosnick drove in three. Mike Rokovich added a triple of his own. All 11 Franklin batters recorded hits — not a single out made at the plate across a 24-hit, 14-run performance. Still not enough.

Paul Besse and Joe Bandel quietly provided the margin — 5 combined RBIs, just enough cushion to hold on when Franklin threatened late. A different bounce, a different at-bat, and the standings look entirely different. This Franklin team isn’t rebuilding anymore. They’re competing.
week1-game2:
Lincoln Lions 8, Burlingame Expansion 3 — Chris Lau didn’t make a single out. Three trips to the plate, three hits, two doubles, two runs scored. That kind of top-of-the-order production sets a tone, and Lincoln Lions followed it all the way to a controlled 8-3 wire-to-wire win over Burlingame Expansion.

The Lions used everybody. Mike Benveniste drove in a team-high 3 runs. Peter Ou added 2 RBIs out of the eighth spot. Barlow Gilmore, Arjun Moorthy, and Kenny Kim each delivered multi-hit games. Nine of Lincoln’s 13 batters reached base. There’s no soft spot in this lineup — no place to hide, no free out to be had anywhere in the order.

Jack Maguire gave the Expansion something to cheer about, going a perfect 3-for-3 with all 3 of his team’s RBI in a performance completely lost in the final score. The rest of the Expansion lineup went 6-for-26. Seven batters went hitless. For a team of alumni who aged out of the other programs in the league, the gap between where they are and where they need to be showed up clearly in the box score.

Lincoln is 1-0 and looks every bit the contender they were built to be. The Expansion’s path back to relevance is going to take some time.
week1-game3:
Hoover 17, McKinley 2 2 — There was never a moment this felt close. Hoover dismantled McKinley 2 from the first inning, piling up 19 hits in a statement-making 17-2 victory that showcased exactly the offensive depth that made them playoff contenders last fall.

Phillip Koblis led the onslaught from the top of the order — three hits, a double, and 4 runs scored, a constant presence that forced McKinley pitching to make perfect pitches that never came. Sean Lowenthal drove in 4 from the cleanup spot. Adam Ramirez doubled, drove in 3, and crossed the plate twice. Jim Szafranski scored 3 times. Levon Stepanian, Sunil Koshie, and Chris Cohendet all added multiple contributions in a lineup with no obvious weak link. Nine of ten Hoover starters reached base at least once.

McKinley 2 was relegated from the higher league and arrived in this division facing a steep adjustment curve. David Conti and Sanjiv Parikh each went 2-for-2, flashing the contact ability that will serve them well as the season develops. But three errors behind them opened the door to extra Hoover damage, and facing a lineup this potent while still finding their footing is about as hard as it gets in this league.

Hoover isn’t just back. They’re better.
week1-game4:
Washington Wildkittens 14, Carey 13 — Every field should have games like this one. Washington and Carey combined for 37 hits and 27 runs in a full-throttle offensive war, and when the final out was recorded, Washington stood on top 14-13 in the most entertaining contest of opening week.

Chris Geheran was the difference. A double, a triple, and a game-high 6 RBIs in a 3-for-4 night that will be referenced in this league for years. Brian Roth went 3-for-4 and scored 3 times. Darryl Saifher collected 3 hits and 3 RBIs. Darren Miles doubled twice and drove in 2. Washington threw everything at Carey and just barely had more.

Because Carey could play, too. Marc Acton and Ryan Batenchuck each went a perfect 3-for-3 and scored three times apiece — Batenchuck hit two doubles and looked like the best hitter on the field for stretches. Chris Coleman drove in 3. Travis Barabin added 3 RBIs with a double of his own. Carey — relegated from the higher league and facing a steep adjustment to this division — scattered 17 hits and trailed by just one run in the final inning. They ran out of outs.

Washington is 1-0. Carey is 0-1 and already has more offensive firepower than that record suggests.
week2-game1:
St. Catherines 25, McKinley 2 0 — Somewhere around the 15th hit, it stopped being a game and became a history lesson. St. Catherines delivered the most dominant performance of the young season, shutting out McKinley 2 by a 25-0 count in a surgical team offensive display where every single Tiger who stepped to the plate reached base.

Paul Besse was the centerpiece of an evening that defied reasonable expectations: 3-for-3, 5 RBIs, 3 runs scored, 2 triples. Mo Tancilau went 3-for-3 with two doubles. Matt Germino scored three times without making an out. Ray Malaspina collected 3 hits and scored 3. Joe Bandel drove in 4. James Lin added 3 RBIs. Art Wong, Danny Bahamondes, and Ricky Gomez each went 2-for-2. All 15 St. Catherines batters reached base at least once. There was nowhere for McKinley to hide and no pause in the pressure from the first inning to the last.

McKinley managed exactly 2 hits — singles by Brandon Wright and Sanjiv Parikh — and despite reaching base, never crossed the plate. The shutout was the inevitable conclusion to a talent gap that was apparent from the opening at-bat.

St. Catherines has scored 40 runs in two games. They’re not just good. They’re on a different level entirely.
week2-game2:
Franklin 20, Carey 8 — Whatever doubts lingered about the Falcons after a competitive Week 1 result, Franklin put them to rest in emphatic fashion on Wednesday evening. A 20-8 dismantling of Carey featured one of the most diverse and sustained offensive performances of the young spring season — a lineup operating in near-perfect concert with contributions from top to bottom.

Jonah VanZandt was the headline, going 3-for-4 with two triples and a game-high five RBIs — a line that stands alone in the box score and deserves its own paragraph. Ryan Pierce matched the energy in a different way, reaching base all four trips, going 4-for-4 with two doubles, three runs scored, and four RBIs. Steven Jefferson went a perfect 4-for-4 with two runs and two RBIs. Todd Lanam laced two doubles in a 3-for-4 night and scored twice. Robby Samuelson went 3-for-4 with two RBIs. Jason Sosnick doubled and drove in one. Every Franklin starter reached base at least twice, and the Falcons sent the lineup around multiple times in what became an extended offensive exercise.

Carey — relegated from the higher league and still adjusting to the pace of competition in this division — showed flashes of the lineup that earned them a promotion in the first place. Marc Acton went 2-for-3 and scored twice from the top of the order. Pudge Colaco tripled and drove in a run. Matthew Meister went 2-for-2 with an RBI. Rob O’Hare tripled too. But sustaining offensive pressure against Franklin’s pitching proved beyond Carey’s reach on this evening. They put up 8 runs, they had their hits, and they still lost by 12. Franklin is going to be a problem for this entire division.
week2-game3:
Hoover 15, Washington Wildkittens 14 — Marc Snyder was the only player on either team to go 4-for-4. In a game with 45 combined hits, two lineups capable of beating anyone, and a one-run final margin, that single distinction told the story of how Hoover escaped with their second straight narrow victory.

Snyder tripled, drove in 3, and scored twice. Cayman Seacrest launched a home run and a double in a 3-for-4 night that produced 3 RBIs and 2 runs. Phillip Koblis doubled twice and drove in 2. Bryan Dow went 3-for-4 with a double and 2 RBIs. Fred Fabor scored twice. Colin Bryant added 3 hits and 2 RBIs. Every single Hoover starter reached base, and the collective output just barely cleared the bar when it needed to.

Washington made them earn every run. Gareth Adams was extraordinary — 3-for-4 with a triple and 5 RBIs, putting up numbers that win most games. Josh Mello drove in 3 on 3 hits. Drew Simmons went 3-for-4 and scored twice. Kentaro Matsurra drew two walks and crossed the plate twice in a quietly impactful performance. Washington’s 14 runs and 19 hits would have beaten almost any other team in this league. Hoover is apparently the exception.

Two games. Two one-run wins. Whatever Hoover is doing right now, it’s working.
week2-game4:
Lincoln Lions 8, Roosevelt Blue 6 — This one didn’t come easy. Lincoln made it 2-0 on the season with an 8-6 win over a Roosevelt Blue squad that pushed them to the final out, grinding out a victory that looked more like a fight than a formality.

Mike Benveniste did the heavy lifting again — 2-for-3, 2 runs, an RBI, back-to-back multi-hit performances to open the season. Francisco Martinez drove in 2 with a double and scored twice out of the sixth spot. Alan Ching and Peter Ou combined to go 4-for-4, the kind of production from the bottom of the order that gives Lincoln the depth to outrun deficits. Seven different Lions drove in at least one run. In a lineup this complete, there’s no single player you can pitch around.

Roosevelt refused to go quietly. Ankush Bhargava drove in 3 runs on a single hit — a clutch, high-leverage performance that briefly made this a different game. David Vinca and Nick Adler each went 2-for-3 and scored. Joe Carvillo crossed the plate twice. Roosevelt had the opportunities, stranded too many runners, and couldn’t string together the hits needed to erase the deficit when it mattered most.

Lincoln looks like the real deal. Roosevelt Blue needs a win in the worst way.
week3-game1:
McKinley 2 7, Roosevelt Blue 6 — McKinley 2 escaped with a one-run win Wednesday night, holding off a late Roosevelt Blue rally to snap a two-game losing streak. Rob Whittier set the tone early with a double, a triple, and two runs scored, and Justin Williams delivered the decisive blow with a two-run performance in the final frame to seal it.

McKinley got production throughout the lineup. Williams went 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI, Doug Dabrik was a perfect 3-for-3 to keep rallies alive, and David Conti ripped two doubles to fuel the middle innings. Darwin Rodriguez and Mark Sparhawk each chipped in a run scored as McKinley scratched and clawed to their first win of the spring.

Roosevelt Blue had plenty of chances. Carlos Ortega went 2-for-4 with a double and two RBIs, Joe Carvillo added two runs and a knock, and Chris Frank ripped three hits. But the Bulls left too many runners stranded in the late innings. Roosevelt falls to 0-2 and is still searching for their first win of the season.
week3-game2:
Washington Wildkittens 10, Burlingame Expansion 6 — Washington evened their record at 2-1 Wednesday night, riding a balanced attack to a four-run victory over Burlingame Expansion. Chris Sandell led the charge with three hits, a double, and three runs scored, while Brian Roth went 3-for-4 with a double, a triple, and two RBIs as Washington spread the damage across their entire lineup.

Kentaro Matsurra was just as impressive, going 3-for-4 with two runs scored, and Chris Geheran added three hits and an RBI. Washington strung together multi-hit innings throughout the night, making it difficult for Expansion to find any momentum on the mound. The Wildkittens’ patient approach at the plate paid off, scoring in six of their ten innings at the plate.

Burlingame Expansion battled but couldn’t keep pace. Martin Camacho went 3-for-3 with a double and two runs scored, and Nolan Gallant tripled and drove in two. Jason Lasky had two hits and two RBIs, and Rudy Jauregui added two hits and a run. Expansion falls to 0-2, still looking for their first win with a tough schedule ahead.
week3-game3:
St. Catherines 22, Hoover 21 — In the highest-scoring game of the young spring season, St. Catherines escaped with a one-run thriller Wednesday night, holding off a furious Hoover comeback to stay perfect at 3-0. Ricky Gomez was the night’s MVP, going 4-for-5 with a double and six RBIs, single-handedly keeping St. Cath ahead when Hoover threatened to take the lead for good.

St. Catherines got a monster performance top to bottom. Ray Malaspina was a perfect 5-for-5 with a double and four runs scored, Ethan Bachwich drew a walk and scored four times, and Trevor Zlatunich drew two more walks to go with a double and three RBIs. Jerry Ng, Art Wong, and James Lin each contributed multi-hit efforts, combining for eight RBIs as the Tigers’ offense kept answering every Hoover surge.

Hoover gave every bit of it back. Fred Fabor slugged a home run, drove in six, and scored three times, while Phillip Koblis went 5-for-5 with a double and five RBIs. Chris Cohendet had four hits and four RBIs, and Levon Stepanian and Steve Juno each scored three runs. Hoover falls to 2-1 despite one of the most impressive offensive efforts of the season — they simply ran out of innings.
week3-game4:
Lincoln Lions 20, Franklin 11 — Lincoln Lions rolled to their third straight win Wednesday night, pounding Franklin with a relentless 20-hit attack to move to 3-0 on the spring. Francisco Martinez led the way with a perfect 4-for-4 night including a double and three RBIs, while Chris Lau added three hits, a double, a triple, and four RBIs as Lincoln’s top of the order proved too much for Franklin to handle.

Lincoln was a machine from first pitch. Elliot Katz tripled and scored three times, Brett Reynolds went 2-for-3 with a double and four RBIs, and Mike Benveniste went 3-for-4 with three runs. Arjun Moorthy hit safely three times and drove in two, and Jeff Kloster added two hits and two RBIs. Fourteen Lions reached base, and 13 different batters contributed to the scoring.

Franklin made it interesting despite playing shorthanded, missing three regulars at key positions. Mike Rokovich launched a two-run home run and drove in four, and Robby Samuelson went a scalding 4-for-4 with a double. Alex Liu drew two walks, had two hits, and scored twice, and Ed LaGory chipped in a pair of hits and two runs. The Falcons showed heart with a depleted roster, but had no answers for Lincoln’s loaded lineup. At full strength, this one could look very different — Franklin falls to 1-2 and will need those players back soon.
week4-game1:
St. Catherines 18, Lincoln Lions 5 — The Tigers came into Lincoln’s house and made themselves right at home, pounding out 24 hits in a dominant road win Monday night at Bayside Park. Trevor Zlatunich led the assault, going 4-for-5 with a triple, a home run, and five RBIs, while Paul Besse matched him with a 4-for-5 line of his own including a homer and four driven in. St. Catherines has now won four straight to open the season, outscoring opponents 80-40.

Denzel McCallum set the table all night, scoring three times in his first start. DeLosSantos, Danny Bahamondes, and Mo Tancilau each contributed multi-hit games as the Tigers worked through a deep lineup with ease. St. Cath finished with no errors and five walks drawn, putting pressure on the Lincoln defense at every turn.

The Lions managed nine hits and five runs, getting contributions from Elliot Katz (2-for-3, 2 R) and Mike Benveniste (2-for-2, D, 2 BI), but it was never close after the early innings. Barlow Gilmore provided the highlight for Lincoln with a triple and two RBIs. The Lions fall to 3-1 and will need to regroup quickly in a tight middle of the standings.
week4-game2:
Hoover 23, Burlingame Expansion 3 — Hoover unleashed one of the most dominant offensive performances of the young season Monday night, going 30-for-39 at the plate and cruising to a 23-3 rout of Burlingame Expansion. Bryan Dow was the story, crushing a triple and a home run en route to a jaw-dropping seven RBIs, while Cayman Seacrest went a perfect 5-for-5 with a double and five driven in. The Hoover lineup showed no mercy from the first inning on.

Phillip Koblis (5-for-5), Sunil Koshie (3-for-4, 4 R), Sean Lowenthal (3-for-4, 2 D, 3 R), and Levon Stepanian (3-for-4, 3 R) all had multi-hit nights as Hoover batted around the order repeatedly. Paul Dilaura contributed three hits and two RBIs in what appeared to be his spring debut. The club’s team average for the game was an absurd .769.

Burlingame could manage only three runs despite 11 hits, with Martin Camacho going 2-for-2 with two RBIs to pace the offense. Rudy Jauregui scored twice and drew a walk, and Kurt Soto chipped in a run, but the Expansion simply had no answer for Hoover’s relentless attack. The club falls to 0-3 and will look to find some offense as the season progresses.
week4-game3:
Washington Wildkittens 15, McKinley 2 14 — In the closest game of the night, the Washington Wildkittens escaped with a one-run thriller over McKinley 2 at Bayside Park, holding on 15-14 after a back-and-forth battle that could have gone either way. Josh Mello was Washington’s offensive catalyst, going 2-for-3 with a double and three critical RBI, while Kentaro Matsurra added two hits and two RBIs in crunch time. The Wildkittens improved to 3-1.

Bill Poucher went 3-for-3 with a double, and Darren Miles drew a walk and scored twice as Washington manufactured runs whenever they needed them. Nick Ciccarelli and Darryl Saifher each contributed two hits, and Brian Roth added a triple as the lineup proved just deep enough to weather McKinley’s furious rally.

McKinley 2 had every reason to believe they’d pull it off — Chris Corde blasted a home run and drove in five, and Brandon Wright went 3-for-3 to keep the pressure on. Joaquin Anguera added a triple and two RBIs, and David Conti went 2-for-3 with two runs scored. But the Machines couldn’t push across that final run, dropping to 1-3 in a tight loss that will sting for a while.
week4-game4:
Roosevelt Blue 18, Carey 6 — Roosevelt Blue broke into the win column in emphatic fashion Monday night, hanging 18 runs on Carey to snap a two-game losing streak. Carlos Ortega homered and drove in three, and Chris Frank went 3-for-4 with a triple and three RBIs as Roosevelt’s offense exploded for 27 hits. Ben Shapiro added a two-run homer to cap a night when nearly every Roosevelt bat came alive.

John Kirk went 3-for-4 with a triple and an RBI in his spring debut, and Will Cockle and Joe O’Leary each went 3-for-3 to lead the hit parade. David Vinca added a double and two RBIs, while Bishu Ganguly chipped in two RBIs. New addition Brian Chang went 3-for-4 with two runs scored in his first outing. Roosevelt’s balanced attack was simply too much for Carey’s pitching to contain.

Carey had their moments — Ryan Chow went 3-for-4 with a home run and two RBIs, and Travis Barabin went a perfect 3-for-3 with a double. Newcomer Nick Barr added two hits and two runs scored. But Carey has now dropped to 0-3 and has been outscored 52-27 on the season. The offense will need to find more consistent production across the lineup as the schedule grows tougher.
week5-game1:
Carey 10, Burlingame Expansion 7 — Carey snapped a three-game skid Tuesday night, turning a scrappy 10–7 victory over Burlingame Expansion into their first win of the spring season. Marc Acton ignited the offense with a 2-for-3 effort featuring two doubles and two runs scored, while Ryan Chow provided the late-game lift with a 2-run performance out of the lower order to help put the game away.

Carey spread the damage across the lineup, with Chris Coleman going 3-for-3 with a double and Kevin Wuerfel adding two hits and a run. The patient at-bats of Kyle Morganroth — reaching base twice on sacrifice flies while drawing no strikeouts — kept the line moving in a balanced attack that found contributions from top to bottom.

Burlingame Expansion, still searching for their first win, got a standout night from Martin Camacho, who launched a solo home run to go with his RBI, and Vic Gallant, who went a perfect 3-for-3. Nolan Gallant chipped in two hits including a double and a triple. But the Expansion couldn’t sustain the rally, stranding runners in key spots and falling to 0–4 on the season.
week5-game2:
St. Catherines 15, Roosevelt Blue 3 — St. Catherines kept their perfect record intact with a commanding 15–3 rout of Roosevelt Blue on Tuesday night, as Ray Malaspina turned in the most dominant individual performance of the young season. Malaspina went 3-for-3 with a home run and five RBIs, providing the defining blow in a game that was never close after the first few innings.

The Tigers got production from everywhere in their lineup. Anthony DeLosSantos — making his spring debut — went 3-for-3 with a double and three runs scored, while CJ Nunez added a clutch pinch-hit home run late in the game. Joe Bandel drove in a run with a triple, and Denzel McCallum collected two hits including a double. St. Catherines now sit alone atop the standings at 5–0, showing no signs of slowing down.

Roosevelt Blue managed just nine hits on the night and scored three runs, with David Ding going 2-for-2 as the lone bright spot in an otherwise quiet offensive showing. Joe Carvillo added a run scored, and Carlos Ortega drew a walk to reach base. The Blue fall to 1–3 and face a tough road ahead to climb back into contention.
week5-game3:
Franklin 22, Washington Wildkittens 21 — Down 11–0 after Washington sent a crooked number up on the board in the top of the first, Franklin staged one of the most improbable comebacks of the season, clawing back run by run before walking it off in the bottom of the final inning on a Mu Jing sacrifice fly to complete the 22–21 thriller. Jing finished 2-for-4 with two RBIs, but none bigger than the walk-off sac fly that capped the stunning turnaround.

Todd Lanam led the Falcons’ relentless charge with four hits — three doubles and a triple — and four RBIs, while Ryan Pierce went 4-for-5 with two triples and Jonah VanZandt added four hits and three RBIs. At the bottom of the order, Ed LaGory was quietly perfect, going 4-for-4 with a triple and two runs scored to keep Franklin’s innings alive when it mattered most.

Washington’s Chris Geheran was spectacular in a losing effort, going 5-for-5 with two doubles and five RBIs — doing much of the damage in that devastating first inning. Kentaro Matsurra went 3-for-4 with three runs scored and Nick Ciccarelli drove in four. The Wildkittens fall to 3–2, their offense clearly capable of scoring with anyone — but unable to hold what looked like an insurmountable lead.
week5-game4:
Hoover 14, Lincoln Lions 3 — Hoover dismantled the Lincoln Lions 14–3 Tuesday night in a wire-to-wire performance that reaffirmed their status as one of the top teams in the league. Brad Null led the way with a perfect 5-for-5 night and two RBIs, while Jim Szafranski went 4-for-5 with three runs scored and an RBI in a balanced attack that had every slot in the order contributing.

Christian DiCarlo was especially productive, drawing two walks and driving in four runs despite just one hit, while Sean Lowenthal added two hits and three RBIs. Paul Dilaura added a triple and two RBIs as Hoover’s potent offense rolled to 4–1 on the season. The pitching-defense combination held Lincoln in check all night, never allowing a sustained rally.

Lincoln got three hits and two runs from Francisco Martinez, who went 3-for-3 with two doubles, and Chris Lau chipped in two RBIs. But the Lions couldn’t generate enough traffic against a Hoover squad that looked sharp in every phase. Lincoln falls to 3–2, and will need a bounce-back performance to stay in the hunt at the top of the standings.
week6-game1:
Franklin 13, Hoover 10 — In a hard-fought makeup game on a warm Thursday night, the Franklin Falcons snapped a four-game skid with a gritty 13–10 upset of the Hoover squad, spoiling what had been one of the league’s stoutest records. Todd Lanam set the tone with a 4-for-4 night including a double and 2 RBI, while Jason Sosnick added 3 hits and 2 doubles to fuel a relentless Franklin attack.

The Falcons got contributions up and down the lineup. Nate Lawler went 3-for-4 with 2 runs, Mike Rokovich added 3 hits and a double, and Mu Jing drove in 2 runs to help Franklin maintain the lead in the late innings. Ed LaGory’s RBI triple provided some crucial insurance, and Robby Samuelson and Jonah VanZandt each chipped in with clutch hits as Franklin sent 11 players to the plate with at least one knock.

Hoover fought back gamely — Cayman Seacrest went 3-for-5 with 2 runs, and Sean Lowenthal and Sunil Koshie each notched 3 hits — but the Falcons’ offense proved too deep to overcome. The loss drops Hoover to 5–2, while Franklin climbs to 3–4 and back into the playoff conversation.
week6-game2:
St. Catherines 20, Washington Wildkittens 1 — The St. Catherines Tigers served notice to the rest of the league Thursday night, rolling to a lopsided 20–1 rout of the Washington Wildkittens to push their record to a dominant 6–1. Joe Bandel was the headliner, going 3-for-4 with 2 doubles, a home run, and a staggering 6 RBI in a performance that had onlookers shaking their heads.

It was a collective statement from the Tigers lineup. Anthony DeLosSantos went 4-for-4 with 3 runs, Paul Besse added 3 hits and 3 runs, and Andrew Phu and Jerry Ng each went 3-for-3 to keep the pressure relentless. Denzel McCallum added 2 hits and 2 RBI, and Tim Driscoll and CJ Nunez also scored as St. Catherines cycled through a deep, balanced attack.

Washington managed just one run on eight hits, with Darryl Saifher going 3-for-3 and Kentaro Matsurra adding 2 hits as the lone bright spots in an otherwise forgettable night for the Wildkittens. Washington falls to 3–5 and faces a steep climb in the standings with only a few weeks left.
week6-game3:
Roosevelt Blue 14, Burlingame Expansion 7 — Roosevelt Blue moved back to .500 and above with a convincing 14–7 win over Burlingame Expansion on Thursday night, fueled by a balanced attack from top to bottom. Ankush Bhargava led the charge with a 4-for-4 performance including a triple and 3 RBI, while Nick Adler matched that with 4 hits, a triple, and 2 RBI of his own.

Roosevelt Blue got production all night. Joe Carvillo added 3 hits, a double, and 2 RBI, Will Cockle went 3-for-4 with an RBI, and Dave Tobias added 3 runs despite going hitless — a testament to a patient, run-manufacturing offense. Carlos Ortega went 3-for-4 with a run batted in, and David Ding added a run-scoring triple to cap off a well-rounded team effort.

For Burlingame Expansion, Nolan Gallant kept things interesting with a 2-hit performance capped by a home run and 4 RBI, and Vic Gallant went 3-for-3 with 2 RBI. But the Expansion struggled to string together rallies, and Roosevelt Blue’s depth proved the difference. Burlingame falls to 2–5 while Roosevelt Blue improves to 4–3.
week6-game4:
Carey 17, McKinley 2 16 — Thursday night produced the thriller of the week, as Carey held on for a white-knuckle 17–16 victory over McKinley 2 in the makeup game of the postponed Week 6. Ryan Batenchuk was electric for Carey, going 3-for-3 with 2 doubles and 3 RBI, while Michael Boice capped a 3-for-3 night with a home run and 2 RBI to provide the margin in a game that came down to the final outs.

Carey had multiple heroes: Pudge Colaco went 3-for-3 with 3 RBI, Marc Acton added 3 hits and 2 doubles, and John Allan went 2-for-2 with a walk and 2 runs scored. Robert Jan de Voogd had a perfect 3-for-3 game with a double and 2 RBI, and Travis Barabin drove in a run with a triple to round out an offense that just barely did enough.

McKinley 2 made it a game all the way through, getting a breakout night from new face Colin Sullivan, who went 3-for-4 with a double, a triple, and 5 RBI. Sanjiv Parikh added 3 hits and 3 RBI, Rob Whittier went 3-for-4 with 2 runs, and Connor Lundy notched 3 hits and 2 doubles. McKinley 2 falls to 1–5–1; Carey evens their record at 3–4.
week7-game1:
Burlingame Expansion 26, Franklin 10 — Burlingame Expansion delivered one of the most lopsided performances of the spring season Wednesday night, erupting for 26 runs to hand Franklin its third loss and first blowout of 2026. Nolan Gallant was the unstoppable force at the top of the order, going a perfect 5-for-5 with a triple, a home run, and three RBI, while Vic Gallant added three hits, a triple, and three RBI out of the six hole. The Expansion offense spread the carnage across the lineup — ten of eleven batters reached base, with Rudy Jauregui (3-for-5, 3 R) and Matt Easterday (1-for-4, 4 R) setting the pace.

Burlingame improved to 1-4 on the season, but this result snapped an 0-4 skid in emphatic fashion. Bob Kraska went 3-for-3 with two doubles and four RBI from the nine hole, and Jason Lasky scored four runs himself despite going 2-for-4. No pitcher in this league will look forward to seeing this lineup at full strength.

Franklin had no excuses on this night — Todd Lanam went 3-for-4 with two doubles and Uland Wong added three hits and two runs, but the Falcons were simply outmatched by an Expansion squad firing on all cylinders. Jonah VanZandt chipped in two hits and two RBI, and the Falcons fall to 2-3, now fighting to stay above .500 in the back half of the schedule.
week7-game2:
Lincoln Lions 14, McKinley 2 14 (Tie) — In one of the most dramatic finishes of the spring, Lincoln Lions and McKinley 2 played to a 14-14 deadlock Wednesday night, splitting a point each in the standings and leaving both clubs hungry for more. Arjun Moorthy was Lincoln’s engine, delivering a 3-for-3 night with three doubles and four RBI, while Mike Benveniste matched him step for step — 3-for-3, two doubles, three runs, and two RBI. It was a statement showing for a Lions lineup that had been held to three runs in their week 5 loss to Hoover.

McKinley 2 refused to fold, with Brandon Wright going 3-for-3 with a double, a home run, and three RBI, and Darwin Rodriguez adding three hits and three RBI out of the three hole. Doug Dabrik chipped in two hits, two doubles, and four RBI to keep the Monarchs in striking distance all night. Both teams left 28 combined runs on the night, with neither able to pull away.
